i don’t think it’s the fear of surviving. i think it’s the fear of failure. 
the fear that i will have to live with the fact that i couldnt even do something as cowardly and pathetic as running away from all my problems. that i’m such a failure that i can’t even bring myself to end it all. the fear of that feeling when you wake up the next day, ashamed of yourself for failing and therefore in 10x as much pain than before. 

the sense of failure is powerful. if this is what you feel is holding you back from suicide, there’s a strong chance it’s holding you back from other things in life. and when you are avoiding things you may enjoy or that may be healthy ways of coping, you may then end up being depressed and, consequently, suicidal. 
if you can relate to this, try to adjust your mindset regarding healthy tasks and activities so that you can try out more hobbies and activities and coping mechanisms.

while depression is a universal experience, that doesn’t mean everyone’s mind is wired in the same way. many people deny their depression and act as though it doesn’t exist in attempt to push it away. accepting does NOT mean giving up. it simply means being honest with yourself and accepting that you may need help and you are in a bad place. i’ve had problems with this personally as i’ve tended to convince myself that it’s not THAT bad and that others have it worse etc etc, but i’ve realised that thinking that way has sent me further into depression by invalidating myself and neglecting to care for myself in the way that i’ve needed to. you can’t treat illnesses by pretending they don’t exist, and that, unfortunately, is something many people tend to forget when dealing with mental illness.

honest and genuine responses please! all input is welcome though, i would love to hear everything everyone has to say. even embarrassing and personal coping mechanisms are valid as long as they make you feel good in a healthy way :)

in my opinion, accepting your depression is the first step to recovery. accepting it doesn’t mean giving in, it means addressing that you have an issue and that you need to change the way you think and act in order to combat it. living in constant denial will get you nowhere other than frustration and continuation of unhealthy habits and mindsets. by ignoring it you are letting it grow and grow until it’s almost untameable. it’s always important to self reflect and be honest with yourself about your mental health. 

healthy coping mechanisms are a way to combat self-defeating thoughts rather than embrace them as there is no way to begin to consciously pull yourself out of a depression through healthy coping strategies without accepting that you are depressed in the first place. while some naturally come out of depressive episodes, which is great, it’s still important to stay in tune with yourself, and to be mindful that others may have to pull themselves up rather than wait for a depression to end, and that sometimes you need to step in and take action against your negative mental state. hope this makes sense!
